name: Executive order of November 1867 changing the Niobrara (Santee Sioux) reservation
aka: Expanding Sioux Indian Reservation in Nebraska (1867)
citation: Executive Order of November 15, 1867 (Royce dates it November 16, 1867)
promises: Township 32 north, range 4 west, and parts of fractional township 33 north, range 4 west, adjoining the reservation on the Niobrara and Missouri rivers, were withdrawn from market and set apart for the use of the Santee Sioux.
Fractional township 32 north, range 6 west, until then part of the reservation, was restored to market.
landTaken: Royce shows fractional township 32 north, range 6 west (area 514) as relinquished by this order; it had been withdrawn for the Santee by the order of February 27, 1866.
today: Royce lists further changes to the Niobrara reservation by executive orders of August 31, 1869 and later.

openQuestions: The American Presidency Project dates the Secretary's letter and the President's approval November 15, 1867; Royce and treaties.json give November 16, 1867.
Not a treaty: an executive order adjusting a reservation set up by executive order, adding land and returning one fractional township. Under the 2026-11-08 rule this is not by itself a breach.
The ICC title search for "santee" returned only the 1974 Sioux Nation (Black Hills) dockets; no Commission or court finding about this tract was located.
The Santee Sioux Nation's own history of the Niobrara reservation was not found online.
2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for: Court of Claims names "santee" (0); ICC full text "Santee Niobrara", "Niobrara" (no decision on the 1867 order). Nothing new.
